title: Your Korean friend texts “보고 싶어”… don’t send selfies 😳 #learnkorean
caption:
보고 싶어 (bo-go si-peo) = I miss you 💗
Word by word it’s 보다 (to see) + -고 싶다 (want to) — “I want to see you” — but in a text it means “I miss you.”

How to reply:
나도 보고 싶어 (na-do bo-go si-peo) = I miss you too
More polite: 보고 싶어요 (bo-go si-peo-yo)

pinnedComment: Who would you text “보고 싶어” to? 👇 (a friend? mom? your bias? 😉)
alt: A needle-felt miniature bedroom at night. It opens on a floating lilac phone bursting dozens of felt polaroid selfies of Mongle, a coral felt ghost-like mascot, with “+37 photos sent”, then rewinds 10 seconds: a Korean friend texts 보고 싶어~. Word by word, 보고 = see and 싶어 = want to, so Mongle thinks “She wants to SEE me? Photos!”, poses for flashing selfies and sends a flood of polaroids. A close-up shows the friend doll on a mint phone laughing behind her hands: ㅋㅋㅋ (lol) 아니 그게 아니라… (no, that’s not what I meant). Mongle goes flat and red with embarrassment as the card explains 보고 싶어 means I miss you. Mongle replies 나도 보고 싶어 (I miss you too) with rising hearts, sends a few more selfies, and asks who you would text 보고 싶어 to.
